children.translated_text: The practitioner of rasa who first studies the chapter on definitions
is never confused in understanding the meaning of the <s>rasatantra</s> (science of mercury and alchemy).
That which illuminates meanings that are hidden, unexpressed, only slightly stated, or doubtful,
and whose meaning is firmly ascertained, is called by the learned a <s>paribhāṣā</s> (technical definition).

children.text: saindhavaṃ cātha sāmudraṃ viḍaṃ sauvarcalaṃ tathā
children.translated_text: Rock salt, sea salt, <s>viḍa</s>, and likewise <s>sauvarcala</s>,
and <s>romaka</s>: these five should be known by the wise as the five salts.
Sindhu-born salt, <s>rucaka</s>, and <s>pākya</s>: this is remembered as the three salts;
or it is proclaimed as the triad of salts, the set of three salts.
Among these too, rock salt is declared by the learned to be the chief one;
when salt is mentioned in general, rock salt should be employed.
<s>Svarjikṣāra</s> and <s>yavakṣāra</s> are stated to be the two alkalis;
when joined with <s>saubhāgya</s>, they are stated to be the triad of alkalis.
<s>Muṣkakṣāra</s>, <s>yavakṣāra</s>, <s>kiṃśukakṣāra</s>,
<s>svarjikṣāra</s>, and <s>tilakṣāra</s> are called the five alkalis.
Those produced from lime, palāśa tips, tamarind, arka, and sesame stalks,
together with <s>svarjikā</s> and barley-spike alkali, are stated to be the eight alkalis.
The urines of the buffalo, goat, sheep, elephant, donkey, camel, horse,
are stated by the foremost physicians to be the eight urines.
For donkey, elephant, camel, and horse, the urine of males is praised;

children.text: go'jāvimahiṣīṇāṃ ca mūtraṃ strīṇāṃ hitaṃ matam ||
children.translated_text: for cow, goat, sheep, and buffalo, the urine of females is considered beneficial.
Among all urines, cow urine is the most endowed with qualities;
therefore, when no special distinction is stated, cow urine should be used.

children.text: gokhuraistāḍitaṃ goṣṭhe śuṣkaṃ cūrṇopamaṃ ca yat
children.translated_text: That dried material in a cow pen, struck by the hooves of cows and resembling powder,
is called cow dung by the wise, known by the name <s>govara</s>.
<s>Jambīra</s>, <s>nimbuka</s>, sour vetasa, tamarind,
orange, pomegranate, tree-sorrel, and citron,
<s>cāṅgerī</s>, chickpea sourness, jujube, <s>karamardaka</s>,
and <s>cukrikā</s>: in general these are proclaimed as the class of acidic substances.
With sour vetasa, jambīra, <s>luṅga</s>, orange, and nimbuka,
the five fruit-acids are known, and they are called the five acids.
With the juices of jujube, pomegranate, tree-sorrel, cāṅgerī, and tamarind,
the five acids are named, indeed the set of five acidic substances.
Of all kinds of acidic substances, nimbūka is the most endowed with qualities;
or sour vetasa, or tamarind, is superior in qualities.
<s>Guḍūcī</s>, bark of neem root, <s>bhiṣaṅmātā</s>, <s>nidigdhikā</s>,
and the leaf of <s>paṭola</s>: this is proclaimed as the five bitters.
Brick powder, ash, likewise earth from an anthill,
red ochre, and salt: these are called the five earths.

children.text: ājyaṃ guḍo mākṣikaṃ ca vijñeyaṃ madhuratrikam
children.translated_text: Ghee, jaggery, and honey should be known as the sweet triad;
it is also regarded as the three sweets, and likewise the set of three sweet substances.

children.text: gavyaṃ kṣīraṃ dadhi ghṛtaṃ mākṣikaṃ cātha śarkarā
children.translated_text: Cow's milk, curd, ghee, honey, and sugar
are named the five nectars, effective in accomplishing rasa procedures.

children.text: gavyaṃ kṣīraṃ dadhi ghṛtaṃ gomūtraṃ gomayaṃ tathā
children.translated_text: Cow's milk, curd, ghee, cow urine, and cow dung,
combined together in equal measure, are here called the five cow-products.
The milk of <s>ravi</s>, the milk of banyan, and the milk of <s>snuhī</s>,
are known as the three milks and are praised in killing and similar operations.
Female elephant, mare, cow, ewe, she-goat, she-camel,
buffalo cow, she-ass, woman, <s>kākodumbarikā</s>, and <s>sudhā</s>,
<s>dugdhikā</s>, udumbara, arka, banyan, aśvattha, and tilvaka:
with the milks of these, the class of milks is concisely named.
Oils born from sesame, mustard, <s>unmatta</s>, bhallātaka, castor, and neem,
and the oils of flax and others are accepted here as the class of oils.

children.text: nirdravairdhātubhiścātha gandhādibhiḥ peṣitaḥ pāradaḥ ślakṣṇatāṃ prāpitaḥ
children.translated_text: Mercury, ground with dry metals and with substances such as sulphur, and brought to smoothness,

children.text: kajjalābho yadā jāyate'sau tadā nāmataḥ kovidaiḥ kajjalītyucyate ||
children.translated_text: when it becomes like collyrium, is then called by experts by the name <s>kajjalī</s>.

children.text: kajjalī kajjalaṃ caiva matā kajjalikā ca sā
children.translated_text: It is regarded as <s>kajjalī</s>, <s>kajjala</s>, and also <s>kajjalikā</s>;
and it is especially prescribed at the beginning of preparing rasa substances.
Mercury ground with moist substances such as sulphur and with metals,
very smooth and resembling mud, is remembered as <s>rasapaṅka</s> (mercurial paste).
Having triturated <s>sūta</s> (mercury) with sulphur and with liquids such as milk,

children.text: peṣaṇātpiṣṭatāṃ nītā matā piṣṭī ca piṣṭikā ||
children.translated_text: when it is brought to the state of a paste by grinding, it is regarded as <s>piṣṭī</s> and <s>piṣṭikā</s>.
Mercury produced from cinnabar by means of an upward-sublimation apparatus
is remembered as <s>hiṅgulottha</s> and is called <s>hiṅgulākṛṣṭa</s>.
When diamond and the like are blown in a furnace together with melting drugs,
the essence that comes out is here designated <s>sattva</s>.
The essence produced from forest herbs by means of a steam-sweating apparatus
is called <s>sattva</s> by those skilled in the <s>rasatantra</s>.
Wax and sesame oil, mixed in the prescribed proportion,
cooked until it resembles fresh butter, is proclaimed as <s>sikthataila</s> (wax-oil).

children.text: guñjā madhu guḍaḥ sarpiḥ saubhāgyaṃ guggulustathā
children.translated_text: <s>Guñjā</s>, honey, jaggery, ghee, <s>saubhāgya</s>, and guggulu:
this group was taught by earlier teachers as a melter of metals.

children.text: saṃdrāvitasya dravyasya drave nikṣepaṇaṃ tu yat
children.translated_text: The placing of a melted substance into a liquid
is indicated by experts in rasa operations as <s>ḍhālana</s> (pouring or quenching).

children.text: ājyaṃ guñjātha saubhāgyaṃ kṣaudraṃ ca purasaṃjñakam
children.translated_text: Ghee, guñjā, saubhāgya, honey, and what is called <s>pura</s>:
this combination is called by the learned the <s>mitrapañcaka</s> (friendly five).
Especially for the melting of various metals,
the <s>mitrapañcaka</s> is employed by specialists in the <s>rasatantra</s>.
But the casting of another substance into molten tin and the like,
when it is done, is called <s>pratīvāpa</s> and is also termed <s>āvāpa</s>.
The pouring of water and the like upon metal and other substances heated by fire

children.text: sa nirvāpaḥ smṛtaścāpi niṣekaḥ snapanaṃ ca tat ||
children.translated_text: is remembered as <s>nirvāpa</s>; it is also <s>niṣeka</s> and <s>snapana</s>.
But when the fire is crowded with flames and a white appearance arises,
that time for the extraction of the essence is remembered as the pure revolution, <s>śuddhāvarta</s>.
<s>Kajjalikā</s>, liquefied by contact with fire and flattened on a plantain leaf,

children.text: rasāgamajñaiḥ khalu parpaṭī sā prakīrtitā parpaṭikā ca saiva ||
children.translated_text: is indeed called <s>parpaṭī</s> by those who know the rasa tradition; that same thing is also <s>parpaṭikā</s>.
When, of two metals joined together, one is destroyed
and the refining of the other metal takes place,
then the beating here by blowing with a bent tube is called <s>tāḍana</s>.
A metal that has undergone such beating is proclaimed to be <s>tāḍita</s>, beaten.
When copper, treated with medicines, is beaten with a bent tube
and becomes free of ringing, that copper is here called <s>ghoṣākṛṣṭa</s>, drawn free of sound.
A tube of a hand's length, made of brass and the like,
for giving blasts of air into the fire is called a <s>vaṅkanāla</s>, a bent tube.
That which attains coolness while still situated in the fire
is taught as self-cooled, <s>svāṅgaśīta</s>; it is also considered <s>svataḥśīta</s>.

children.text: vahnerbahiḥ samānīya yad dravyaṃ yāti śītatām
children.translated_text: When a substance is brought out from the fire and becomes cool,
that is taught as externally cooled, <s>bahiḥśīta</s>; it is also considered <s>bāhyaśīta</s>.
The drying, after grinding powdered metal and the like with liquids,

children.text: bhāvanaṃ tanmataṃ vijñair bhāvanā ca nigadyate ||
children.translated_text: is considered by the learned to be <s>bhāvana</s>; it is also called <s>bhāvanā</s>.

children.text: draveṇa yāvatā dravyaṃ cūrṇitaṃ tvārdratāṃ vrajet
children.translated_text: As much liquid as will cause a powdered substance to become moist

children.text: tāvān eva dravo deyo bhiṣagbhir bhāvanāvidhau ||
children.translated_text: just that much liquid should be given by physicians in the procedure of <s>bhāvanā</s>.
A decoction should be made in the same measure as the substance to be impregnated; from that, water eight times as much is used.
The decoction, dried until one-eighth remains, should be used in impregnating with the decoction.
That grinding and similar operation which is performed together with the prescribed medicines
for the cutting away of impurities is here called <s>śodhana</s>, purification.

children.text: mṛtaṃ lohaṃ vinikṣiptaṃ yadā tarati vāriṇi
children.translated_text: When a dead, that is calcined, metal, thrown into water, floats,
that is called water-floating, <s>vāritara</s>, by those well versed in the rasa texts.
When, rubbed between the forefinger and thumb, it enters the spaces between the lines
and, once lodged there, does not come out, that is called dead metal, <s>mṛtaloha</s>.
When dead metal is blown in a heating pit together with silver, ghee, and honey,
and does not abandon its measure of silver, that is called dead metal.

children.text: samitrapañcakaṃ dhmātaṃ prakṛtiṃ naiti yat punaḥ
children.translated_text: When it is blown with the five allies and again does not return to its natural state,
that is said to be free from rebirth, <s>apunarbhava</s>, and it is also called non-rising, <s>niruttha</s>.
When a metal called <s>apunarbhava</s>, combined with silver,
does not stick to silver, that is here called <s>niruttha</s>.
For removing the remaining faults of dead metals and the like,
the process that is performed is considered <s>amṛtīkaraṇa</s>, immortalization.
By means of the apparatus called <s>nāḍikā</s>, through the application of heat from fire,

children.text: binduśo yatsrutaṃ nīraṃ tat parisrutam ucyate ||
children.translated_text: the water that has flowed out drop by drop is called <s>parisruta</s>, distilled.
One should first examine the measure, and then prepare the formula.
For the successful preparation of formulas, measure is now set forth.
By six white mustard seeds one barleycorn is proclaimed.

children.text: tribhir yavaiśca guñjaikā matā saiveha raktikā ||
children.translated_text: By three barleycorns one <s>guñjā</s> is held to be made; that same is here a <s>raktikā</s>.
With <s>raktikās</s> measured as eight in number there is a <s>māṣaka</s>.
With <s>māṣakas</s> numbered as twelve, a <s>tolaka</s> is proclaimed.
The <s>vaṭaka</s>, the <s>kṣudraka</s>, and the <s>draṃkṣaṇa</s> are also proclaimed.
By two <s>tolakas</s> here there is a <s>karṣa</s>; that same is a <s>tinduka</s>.

children.text: akṣaḥ sa eva kathito viḍālapadakaṃ tathā
children.translated_text: That same is called an <s>akṣa</s>, and likewise a <s>viḍālapadaka</s>.
It is also known as a <s>kavalagraha</s>, and is called a <s>suvarṇa</s>.
Two <s>karṣas</s> are a half-<s>pala</s>, and it is called a <s>śukti</s>.

children.text: matā cāṣṭamikā saiva palārdhaṃ ca prakīrtitam ||
children.translated_text: That same is considered an <s>aṣṭamikā</s>, and is proclaimed as half a <s>pala</s>.

children.text: śuktibhyāṃ tu palaṃ jñeyaṃ muṣṭiḥ ṣoḍaśikā ca sā
children.translated_text: By two <s>śuktis</s> one should know a <s>pala</s>; that is a <s>muṣṭi</s> and a <s>ṣoḍaśikā</s>.

children.text: caturthikā ca bilvaṃ ca prakuñcaśca nigadyate ||
children.translated_text: It is also called a <s>caturthikā</s>, a <s>bilva</s>, and a <s>prakuñca</s>.
By two <s>palas</s> one should know a <s>prasṛta</s>; it is also called a <s>prasṛti</s>.
By two <s>prasṛtis</s> there is said to be a <s>kuḍava</s>, and it is remembered as an <s>añjali</s>.
By two <s>kuḍavas</s> there is a <s>śarāva</s>, and it is called a <s>mānikā</s>.
That same is known as eight <s>palas</s> by the wise in rasa doctrine.
Here, with ten <s>palas</s>, the modern <s>sera</s> is remembered.
That same, measured as eighty <s>tolakas</s>, is remembered as the <s>seraka</s>.
One half is the share from perfected mercurial preparations and the like, and likewise from ghee and oil.
But from dead metals and the like it is a quarter, and from an electuary it is an eighth.
A fourth part is from fermented preparations and the like, and a seventh from powders and the like.
For the best physician in this world, out of desire for health and auspiciousness,
the portion that is given by patients, after designating it for <s>Dhanvantari</s>,
has been called by the former teachers the share of <s>Dhanvantari</s>.
The physician who, out of greed, takes more than the share of <s>Dhanvantari</s>

children.text: dadyācca bheṣajaṃ duṣṭaṃ sa vai viśvāsaghātakaḥ ||
children.translated_text: and gives bad medicine is indeed a betrayer of trust.
Here, from the ocean of rasa doctrine and from the jewel-mine and other works,
having selected the priceless jewels of familiar technical definitions,
this very beautiful necklace has been strung with a lovely arrangement.
May it long hang upon the necks of the learned.

children.text: mūṣā hi kumudī khyātā proktā kumudikā ca sā
children.translated_text: The crucible is known as <s>kumudī</s>; it is also called <s>kumudikā</s>.

children.text: krauñcikā vahnimitrā ca pācanī ca nigadyate ||
children.translated_text: It is termed <s>krauñcikā</s>, friend of fire, and <s>pācanī</s>, cooker.
Because it removes faults, therefore it is proclaimed to be a <s>mūṣā</s>, crucible.
Because it resembles a water-lily form, it is also called <s>kumudī</s>.
Since fire is its ally, it is therefore remembered as <s>vahnimitrā</s>.
And because it is fit for cooking substances, it is proclaimed as <s>pācanī</s>.
That which covers a crucible and the like filled with a substance, to prevent the substance from falling out,
is called here a covering, namely a lid.
The smearing with slag and similar materials that is done at the joints of crucibles and the like
is known as joint-smearing; that is also called joint-binding.
The clay that is sandy, pale, long able to withstand the heat of fire,

children.text: sthūlā ca mṛttikā yā syāt mūṣārthaṃ sā matottamā ||
children.translated_text: and coarse, is considered best for making crucibles.
The clay, together with potsherds burned by fire, burnt husks, hemp, and dung, well beaten with a stick,

children.text: yā mṛttikā tadvihitā tu mūṣā sāmānyamūṣā kathitā rasajñaiḥ ||
children.translated_text: from which a crucible is properly made, is called the common crucible by experts in rasa.

children.text: trayo bhāgā mṛdo dvau tu śaṇaladdikayostathā
children.translated_text: There should be three parts of clay, two parts each of hemp and dung,

children.text: bhāgo dagdhatuṣādeśca kiṭṭasya tvardha eva ca ||
children.translated_text: one part of burnt husks and the like, and only half a part of slag.

children.text: ebhiḥ kṛtā tu yā mūṣā vajramūṣā tu sā matā
children.translated_text: The crucible made with these ingredients is regarded as a diamond-crucible,
and it is used especially in the operation of extracting <s>sattva</s> (metallic essence).
Made with husks and the like and with fluxes and the like, and also smeared with them,
this crucible, which accomplishes work with mercury, is called the <s>yogamūṣā</s>.
A crucible constructed from equal parts of earthworm-castings, dung, and the like, and also husks and the like,
together with buffalo milk, is considered one that melts diamond.
The diamond-melting crucible is one that prepares the <s>sattva</s> of diamond;
even when blown upon for two yāmas, it never melts.
The crucible that is made with six-times-burnt dung and with black clay,

children.text: vidhīyate ca kiṭṭādyair gāramūṣā tu sā matā ||
children.translated_text: and with slag and similar materials, is regarded as the dung-crucible.
Even when blown upon for a pair of yāmas, it certainly does not melt.
It is used by experts in rasa especially in pouring and similar procedures.
Provided with a lid, furnished with a crest, and shaped like a cow's udder,
that crucible is regarded as the <s>gostanī</s>, meant for melting and purifying <s>sattva</s>.
When it has been made into the form of a covered capsule by joining two bowls,
it is called the bowl-crucible and is effective for preparing <s>parpaṭī</s> and the like.
The crucible that is round, flattened and broad at the base, and extended in length and breadth,

children.text: vistṛtāsyā ca yā mūṣā mahāmūṣā tu sā matā ||
children.translated_text: and has a wide mouth, is regarded as the great crucible.
For calcining iron, mica, pyrites, <s>sattva</s>, and the like, by the best physicians,

children.text: prayujyate mahāmūṣā sthūlamūṣā ca sā smṛtā ||
children.translated_text: the great crucible is used; it is also remembered as the large crucible.
In the shape of a dhattūra flower, with a perforated tube eight finger-breadths long
firmly attached above, and measuring twelve finger-breadths,
the crucible shaped like an eggplant is the <s>vṛntākamūṣikā</s>.
With this crucible one should prepare the <s>sattva</s> of kharpara and similar substances.
When a substance has become ready to flow because of the application of fire to the crucible,
the brief withdrawal of it is regarded as the replenishing or reviving of the crucible.
It is known as the charcoal-holder, and also as <s>hasantī</s> and <s>hasantikā</s>;
it is likewise called the charcoal-cart and <s>hasanī</s>.
This charcoal-holder is effective for preparing soft substances,
and is used especially in pouring and similar operations for tin and the like.
The small furnace that serves for operations such as extracting <s>sattva</s> and for pouring substances

children.text: vahnisaṃdhānikā yā tu koṣṭhikā sā nigadyate ||
children.translated_text: and that joins with fire is called a <s>koṣṭhikā</s>.
Its height is measured by a royal hand, and its length and breadth are half of that;
it is square in the middle and coated with clay.
It is furnished with a hole measuring four finger-breadths,

children.text: nālikāṃ samakoṇāṃ ca randhre tiryaṅ niveśayet ||
children.translated_text: and one should insert into the hole, crosswise, a tube set at an even angle.
At the mouth of the tube one should place the mouth of the bellows,
and, having filled the furnace with charcoal and placed the substance in its crucible, one should blow it.
It is known as the charcoal-furnace and is effective for pouring substances;
it is used especially for extracting <s>sattva</s>.
One should make a pit in the ground according to rule, one span in breadth,
and in its middle one should prepare a round opening in a low-lying place.
Into the opening in the middle of the pit one should insert a tube crosswise,

children.text: nālavaktre ca bhastrāyā mukhaṃ samyak nirodhayet ||
children.translated_text: and at the mouth of the tube one should properly fasten the mouth of the bellows.
Having placed the substance-crucible in the furnace, one should blow it with the bellows.
This is the subterranean furnace, effective for preparing soft substances.
That which measures the cooking and degree of heat of rasa, subsidiary minerals, metals, and the like,
through contact with a fire of cow-dung cakes and similar fuel, is here remembered as a <s>puṭa</s>.
Because through a <s>puṭa</s> alone there is removal of defects and arising of qualities,
therefore the <s>puṭa</s>-cooking of rasa, subsidiary minerals, and metals is remembered.
By <s>puṭa</s>-cooking, metals and the like become non-revivable, kindled in potency,
and capable of floating on water; therefore it is remembered as <s>puṭa</s>-cooking.
Because, by the procedure of <s>puṭa</s>-cooking, calcined metal and the like surpass calcined mercury,
therefore the <s>puṭa</s> is praised.
When metals and the like that are to be calcined have entered a crucible,
then the sequence of <s>puṭa</s>-heating should be arranged so that the fire suits them properly.
For substances that have been impregnated with juices produced from the herbs used for impregnation,
the drying in the heat of the sun is called a sun-<s>puṭa</s>.
In a square pit two cubits long and half a vyāma deep,
whose interior is filled with forest cow-dung cakes, one should place the crucible filled with what is to be calcined.
Then the expert in rasa should again lay down forest cow-dung cakes and fill the mouth of the pit.

children.text: saṃdīpya vahniṃ puṭanaṃ tatastanmahāpuṭākhyaṃ vibudhaiḥ pradiṣṭam ||
children.translated_text: After lighting the fire, that calcination is prescribed by the learned under the name great-<s>puṭa</s>.

children.text: nṛpakaracaturasrotsedhadairghye tu kuṇḍe chagaṇagaṇabhṛtārdhe mūṣikāṃ sthāpayitvā
children.translated_text: In a pit whose height and length are four royal hands, after placing the small crucible in the half filled with a mass of goat-dung cakes...

children.text: puṭanamiha bhaved yacchāṇapūrṇe 'rdhe bhāge gajapuṭam iha tantre bhāṣitaṃ tad rasajñaiḥ ||
children.translated_text: Here in this tantra the heating called <s>gajapuṭa</s> is said by those who know rasa to be the puṭa in which half the part is filled with dung-cakes.
In a pit of the measure of a cubit, square and likewise raised,
the heating that is given there is called <s>vārāhapuṭa</s>.
In a square depression with a measure of two spans,

children.text: puṭaṃ yad dīyate tattu mataṃ kukkuṭakaṃ budhaiḥ ||
children.translated_text: the heating that is given there is considered <s>kukkuṭaka</s> by the wise.
The heating given on the ground with eight wild dung-cakes
for the accomplishment of mercury and the like is remembered as <s>kapotapuṭa</s>.
The heating that is given by experts with cow-dung cakes or with husks, either in a pit or on the ground,
is remembered as <s>gorvarapuṭa</s>.
When fire is applied to a large vessel filled with husks, with a crucible inside it,
the heating that is given by experts is called <s>bhāṇḍapuṭa</s>.
After firmly placing urine and the like inside heated sand,
the heating that is given there is called <s>vālukāpuṭa</s>.
After placing the <s>kumudikā</s> crucible in the earth and covering it above by two finger-breadths,

children.text: yad dīyate puṭaṃ tattu puṭaṃ bhūdharasaṃjñakam ||
children.translated_text: the heating that is given there is a puṭa called <s>bhūdhara</s>.

children.text: gorvarairvā tuṣairvāpi vitastyūrdhvaṃ puṭaṃ tu yat
children.translated_text: The heating that is done with cow-dung cakes or with husks to a height of one span
for the successful preparation of soft substances is considered <s>lāvakapuṭa</s>.
When specifying the measure of a heating, having considered the strength or weakness of the substance,
one should give whichever one among the puṭas is especially most suitable.

children.text: upalaṃ cotpalaṃ khyātaṃ giriṇḍaṃ piṣṭakaṃ tathā
children.translated_text: An <s>upala</s> is known also as an <s>utpala</s>, and likewise as <s>giriṇḍa</s> and <s>piṣṭaka</s>.

children.text: chāṇaṃ ca chagaṇaṃ caiva karīṣaṃ ca nigadyate ||
children.translated_text: It is also called <s>chāṇa</s>, <s>chagaṇa</s>, and <s>karīṣa</s>.
Since rasa, secondary minerals, metals, and the like are controlled by this
for the accomplishment of calcination and similar operations, therefore it is proclaimed to be a <s>yantra</s>, apparatus.
One should place mercury and the like, which are to be steamed, in cloth threefold in size.
Then, after sealing it with a paste, one should carefully make it into a bundle.
In a vessel filled halfway in its belly with liquids, after making two holes at the mouth and sides,
one should insert a rod there.
In the middle of the rod one should fasten the bundle of substances very firmly.
Following the method shown by the teacher, one should kindle fire below.
Then one should steam it; this is remembered as the <s>dolāyantra</s>.
It is especially employed for the purification and other operations of substances.

children.text: dvādaśāṅgulamukhī suvartulā sudṛḍhā ca khalu garbhavistṛtā
children.translated_text: A pot that has a mouth of twelve finger-breadths, is well-rounded, firm, broad in its interior,
and furnished with a rim of two finger-breadths, is the downward pot in the operation of distillation.
A pot endowed with all the qualities stated, furnished at the bottom with a hole and a firm circular support,

children.text: ūrdhvagā ca jaṭharojjvalā ghaṭī tūrdhvapātanavidhau praśasyate ||
children.translated_text: and going upward, with a blazing belly, is praised in the method of upward distillation.
After placing mercury in the lower pot, one should join the mouths of the two vessels.
Having wrapped and dried the joint, one should then set it on the stove.
After placing a tube in the hole of the circular support, one should coat the joint.
One should pour water into the middle of the support through the opening of the tube.
One should draw out the heated water and put in cold water.
This has been declared by those who know rasa to be the <s>ūrdhvapātanayantra</s>, upward-distillation apparatus.
After smearing mercury inside the upper vessel, one should put water in the lower vessel.

children.text: nikṣipya bhūmau gataṃ ca vidhāya vinyased dṛḍham ||
children.translated_text: Having made it sunk into the ground, one should set it firmly in place.
There one should kindle a strong fire with blazing goat-dung cakes.
This has been declared by those who know rasa to be the <s>adhaḥpātanayantra</s>, downward-distillation apparatus.
One should put the king of rasa, mercury, into a long pot with a bent tube.
With care one should connect that tube into the interior of another jar.
Then one should carefully seal the mouth of the pot containing the mercury.
After that one should kindle a strong fire beneath the mercury-pot.
And one should fill the other pot with clear, cold waters.
This apparatus is called by the name <s>tiryakpātana</s>, lateral distillation.
Here one should obtain a firm, newly made earthen vessel, a span deep.

children.text: bhūtyā tadardhaṃ paripūrya yatnāt tālādigolān kramaśo nidadhyāt ||
children.translated_text: Having carefully filled half of it with ash, one should place balls of orpiment and similar substances in sequence.

children.text: nirdiṣṭabhūtyaiva tadūrdhvabhāgaṃ prapūrya saṃmudrya ca bhāṇḍavaktram
children.translated_text: Having filled the upper part with that same prescribed ash and sealed the mouth of the vessel,

children.text: cullyāṃ nidhāyāgnimatha pradadyādetanmataṃ vai khalu bhasmayantram ||
children.translated_text: one should place it on a stove and then apply fire; this indeed is considered the <s>bhasmayantra</s>, ash apparatus.
After placing mercury in a potsherd inside a vessel filled with water,

children.text: balimadhyagataṃ kumudīnihitaṃ caṣakeṇa bhṛśaṃ pidadhīta tataḥ ||
children.translated_text: and setting it in the middle of the bali and in a <s>kumudī</s>, one should then cover it firmly with a cup.
After sealing the joints with water-clay, one should kindle a fire with khadira charcoal.

children.text: paridīpya bhṛśaṃ supaced gaditaṃ kila kacchapasaṃjñakayantram idam ||
children.translated_text: One should cook it well and intensely; this is said to be the apparatus called <s>kacchapa</s>.
The apparatus called <s>kacchapa</s>, for accomplishing the digestion of bali,
has been described by the teachers of rasa as bestowing success in rasa.
One should cook a <s>kumudī</s> placed in a pit, with all its parts covered with sand,
after covering it with blazing dung-cakes; this is the apparatus called <s>bhūdhara</s>.
The expert in rasa-tantra should skillfully have made a vessel shaped like a mṛdaṅga drum, hollow inside and firm.
It should be made with proper method.
It should be furnished on one side with a turning lid,
and the two side projections should be capable of rotation.

children.text: kārayecca tato yuktyā sūtaṃ gandhaṃ ca nikṣipet
children.translated_text: Then, with proper method, one should put in mercury and sulfur.
And one should fit the turning lid very firmly.

children.text: tato narotsedhamitau stambhau bhūmau tu vinyaset
children.translated_text: Then one should set in the ground two posts of the height of a man.
with the best physician, skilled in procedure, facing it there.
Then he should suspend the apparatus, resting on a rod between the two posts.
This is proclaimed by those who know rasa as the <s>mṛdaṅgayantra</s>, the drum-shaped apparatus.
For making an artificial mleccha, by those skilled in rasa-tantra,
the <s>mṛdaṅgayantra</s> is now especially employed.
Having placed iron and similar substances in a pot, one should cover the mouth with a lid.
One should kindle fire beneath the pot; this is remembered as the <s>sthālīyantra</s>, the pot apparatus.
One should take a glass bottle whose body has been smeared with cloth-pounded clay and dried,
and whose belly is filled with mercury and the like, and set it in place.
Carefully, in a strong pot smeared with clay,
one should fill the bottle there up to its neck with sand.
One should kindle fire beneath the vessel, according to the proper time and sequence.
This has been explained by the wise as the apparatus called <s>vālukāyantra</s>, the sand apparatus.
By depositing salt in the same way, it becomes the <s>lavaṇayantra</s>, the salt apparatus.
It is proclaimed by the best physicians as serving for <s>mṛgāṅka</s> and other rasa preparations.
What is to be roasted in a closed heating should be placed in a jar or the like and covered again
with a firm lid; then one should make a sealing of the joint.
One who knows the measure of fire should cook it in a dung-cake fire or on a stove.
For the calcination of metals and the like, the <s>puṭayantra</s>, the closed-heating apparatus, is praised.
In a vessel whose interior is filled with water, one should place another vessel,
provided on the sides with small openings and filled with a decoction of substances.
Having set it on a stove, one should then kindle the fire below.
Then one should dry the decoction until it comes to the state of powder.
Because steaming is done by vapor, by those skilled in rasa-tantra,
therefore this apparatus is known as the <s>bāṣpasvedana</s>, vapor-steaming apparatus.
This apparatus is said to accomplish the extraction of the essence of particular forest herbs,
for the ease of physicians.
A cup shaped like a ladle and furnished with a long handle
is indeed the <s>darvikāyantra</s>, the ladle apparatus, which accomplishes the purification of sulfur.
This very apparatus, furnished with a bent handle,
is designated by those skilled in rasa-tantra as the <s>pālikāyantra</s>, the small-cup apparatus.
Having set one pot upside down over another pot,
one should cook according to sequence; this apparatus is called <s>ḍamaruka</s>.
In a jar set on a stove, one should put water and the like.

children.text: adhomukhaṃ ghaṭaṃ tvanyaṃ mukhe tasya nidhāpayet ||
children.translated_text: One should place another jar, mouth downward, upon its mouth.
Having smeared the mouths of both with clay, one should then dry them.

children.text: uparisthe tato bhāṇḍe nāḍikāṃ tu niveśayet ||
children.translated_text: Then, in the upper vessel, one should insert a tube.

children.text: etāṃ tu nāḍikāṃ prājñā yatnataḥ kuṇḍalīkṛtām
children.translated_text: The learned should carefully make this tube coiled,
place it in a water trough, pierce it, and then insert it.
At the mouth of a glass bottle one should properly kindle the fire.
until the essence of the substance situated in the jar here becomes vapor.
This indeed is proclaimed by physicians as the <s>nāḍikāyantra</s>, the tube apparatus.
It is especially employed for producing distilled water.
On the ground one should make an excellent pit, one hasta in depth.
Then, having placed a vessel in it, one should take another vessel of the same form.
Then one should put the medicines in that vessel.
One should close its mouth with a saucer whose interior is perforated.
This vessel should be carefully set in the vessel situated in the pit.
One should carefully make a very firm sealing of the joint between the two.

children.text: mṛdā sampūrya gartaṃ tu vahniṃ dadyātprayogavit
children.translated_text: Having filled the pit with clay, the practitioner should apply fire.
Then, when the expert in rasa-tantra knows that it has cooled by itself,

children.text: uparisthaṃ tu vai pātraṃ śanaiḥ samavatārayet
children.translated_text: he should slowly bring down the upper vessel.
He should then collect, according to procedure, the oil that has gone into the lower vessel.
This apparatus has been explained by the wise as the one called <s>pātāla</s>.
It is employed for obtaining the oil of sulfur and similar substances.
A vessel like a cup, very clear, firm, and somewhat unctuous,
made with a hole, is here called the <s>khalvayantra</s>, the mortar apparatus.
For the operations of grinding and the like of rasa, secondary minerals, metals, and so on,
the <s>khalvayantra</s> is employed by those skilled in the procedures of rasa-tantra.
In rasa-tantra the <s>khalvayantra</s> is especially said to be of two kinds:
the first is circular in shape, and the second has the form of a trough.

children.text: vistāre tapanāṃgulaḥ samatalo nīlābjatulyaprabhaḥ nimnatve ca navāṃgulaḥ sumasṛṇo rudrāṅgulocchrāyavān
children.translated_text: In breadth it is twelve finger-breadths, level, with a luster like a blue lotus; in depth it is nine finger-breadths, very smooth, and with a height of eleven finger-breadths.

children.text: bhittyā dvyaṃgulasaṃmitaḥ khalu yathā cendrāṅgulo gharṣakaḥ khalvo'yaṃ khalu vartulo nigaditaḥ sūtādisiddhipradaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Its wall measures two finger-breadths, and the grinder is fourteen finger-breadths; this circular mortar is said to grant success with mercury and the like.

children.text: utsedhe turagāṃgulaḥ khalu kalātulyāṃgulaścāyatau vistāre tapanāṃgulaśca masṛṇo bhittyā ca vai dvyaṃgulaḥ
children.translated_text: In height it is seven finger-breadths, and in length sixteen finger-breadths; in breadth it is twelve finger-breadths, smooth, and with a wall of two finger-breadths.

children.text: gharṣaḥ sūryasamāṃgulaḥ suviśado lohādibhirnirmitaḥ khalvo'yaṃ rasasiddhikṛnnigadito droṇīnibho'tyuttamaḥ ||
children.translated_text: The grinder is twelve finger-breadths, very clear, made of iron and the like; this mortar, resembling a trough, is said to be most excellent and to produce success in rasa.
It is ten finger-breadths in breadth and sixteen finger-breadths in height,
and thirteen finger-breadths in depth, very firm.
It is made of iron and is made very smooth in the middle.
And the iron pestle, beautiful, is twenty finger-breadths long.
This apparatus, called the <s>ulūkhala</s>, is proclaimed by the wise.
This apparatus is employed for pounding tāpya and similar substances.

children.text: laghūni cātha dīrghāṇi yuktyā yantrāṇi kārayet
children.translated_text: And then he should have small and large <s>yantras</s> (apparatuses) made with proper reasoning,
in accordance with the quantity of the substances, being a foremost physician who knows the procedure.
These <s>yantras</s> have been described by me only by way of indication,
for the quick and easy understanding of students who are still beginners.
